title: Interface Specification: the analog-to-digital conversion interface

standards_mappings.rationale: Backs SWE.2 with a real interface specification: providing and consuming module, the real C signature transcribed from the header at 308028fb, per-parameter direction, unit, meaning and valid range with the mechanism that enforces it, a return contract whose values are the enumerators the source defines, validity signalling read off the real error paths, timing where the source imposes one, concurrency, and a required not_specified_by_source list. Two elements over the ADC conversion sequence, and records the shared 10 ms task budget the interface does not expose. The status stays partially_mapped: the whole family remains a reconstruction of an existing implementation rather than the product of an architectural design activity, and Component Design remains absent.

providing_module.name: ADC driver
providing_module.role: Drives the on-chip analog-to-digital converter as a three-state sequence: start the conversion, wait for it to finish, then read the results and publish them. It owns a module-static conversion state and the raw count buffer, and it is the only producer of the measured analogue voltages the supervision path uses.

consuming_modules.name: The 10 ms cyclic task
consuming_modules.consumption_evidence: ADC_Control is called from FTSK_RunUserCodeCyclic10ms at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c L264, in the same function that calls SPS_Ctrl at L265 and SBC_Trigger at L269. The 10 ms task config is anchored at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.h L94.

values.(no return value): The function returns nothing; it advances the conversion state and, when the conversion has finished, publishes the measured voltages to the database.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: A void acquisition entry point gives the caller no way to learn whether a conversion has finished, whether it timed out, or whether the published data is fresh.
return_contract.evidence: src/app/driver/adc/adc.h L94 declares void; src/app/driver/adc/adc.c L118 is the definition.

validity_signalling.mechanism: No return value. The conversion state is module-static and a caller can only observe it through the test accessor.
validity_signalling.evidence: The three-state machine is driven entirely by the module-static adc_conversionState at src/app/driver/adc/adc.c L121; nothing is returned to the 10 ms task that called the function.

timing.evidence: Called every 10 ms from FTSK_RunUserCodeCyclic10ms at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c L264. The source imposes the period by its caller, not by any statement in adc.h.

timeouts.name: ADC conversion latency
timeouts.value: spans at least two calls of the 10 ms task
timeouts.meaning: The conversion sequence needs one call to start, at least one to observe completion, and one to read the results, so a value is published at best three task periods after the start.
timeouts.evidence: The three states are entered in order at src/app/driver/adc/adc.c L122, L127 and L138, each handled once per call, and completion is tested at L129.

concurrency.evidence: Called from the 10 ms cyclic task. The state is module-static and is read-modify-written with no lock, so two concurrent invocations would corrupt the sequence; the source does not guard it.
concurrency.protection_mechanism: none - module-static state written without a lock

error_paths.condition: the conversion does not complete within the expected window
error_paths.observed_behaviour: The state remains ADC_WAIT_CONVERSION_FINISHED and no data is published; the function returns void so the caller is not told.
error_paths.evidence: The completion test is at src/app/driver/adc/adc.c L129 and the state is only advanced when conversionFinished is true at L132-L133.

error_paths.condition: ADC_Control is called twice within one period
error_paths.observed_behaviour: The sequence is advanced twice, potentially reading a conversion that has not finished; the source has no re-entrance guard.
error_paths.evidence: No re-entrance check exists in src/app/driver/adc/adc.c L118-L135.

not_specified_by_source: The interface does not state a timeout for the conversion, so a conversion that never finishes leaves the sequence stuck in ADC_WAIT_CONVERSION_FINISHED indefinitely and nothing reports it.
It does not state the age or freshness of the data it publishes, so a consumer cannot tell a current reading from one left over from a previous sequence.
adc.h carries only the TEST_ADC_* accessors for the conversion state and the voltage table, so the production interface exposes no way to observe this element's progress at all.

values.ADC_START_CONVERSION: The next call will start a conversion.
values.ADC_WAIT_CONVERSION_FINISHED: A conversion has been started and the driver is polling for completion.
values.ADC_CONVERSION_FINISHED: The conversion has completed and the next call will read the results and publish them.

return_contract.default_on_no_information: A read of a module-static state that a caller can interpret; the enumerators are declared at src/app/driver/adc/adc.h L80-L85.
return_contract.evidence: The accessor is declared in the TEST_ADC_ block at src/app/driver/adc/adc.h L100 and defined at src/app/driver/adc/adc.c L161, where it returns the module-static adc_conversionState that ADC_Control switches on at src/app/driver/adc/adc.c L121.

validity_signalling.mechanism: Return value only. This accessor exists solely to let the test harness observe the state, so it is not a production validity channel.
validity_signalling.evidence: Declared among the TEST_ADC_ accessors at src/app/driver/adc/adc.h L98-L101, which the header places in a unit-test-only section.

concurrency.evidence: A unit-test read; not part of the production calling context.

not_specified_by_source: The interface is a test hook, not a production contract, and the record says so rather than presenting it as part of the module's observable interface.
It cannot express a stuck or timed-out conversion, because the state set has no error member.

interface_level_gaps.gap: The conversion sequence has no timeout and no error state, and the production interface has no way to observe it.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: A conversion that never completes leaves the driver in ADC_WAIT_CONVERSION_FINISHED indefinitely, no data is published, and no production consumer can tell that the analogue measurements have gone stale.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: The state machine is src/app/driver/adc/adc.c L118-L135 with the enumerators at src/app/driver/adc/adc.h L80-L85, none of which is an error value; the only state accessor is the test hook at src/app/driver/adc/adc.h L100.

interface_level_gaps.gap: ADC_Control, SPS_Ctrl and SBC_Trigger all run in the same 10 ms task function and none of them reports its own execution time.
interface_level_gaps.consequence: A latency in one of the three lengthens the budget of the others. The task calls them back to back with no timing check between them, so a slow power-path cycle can delay a contactor or SBC action without any of the three reporting it.
interface_level_gaps.evidence: The three calls are at src/app/task/config/ftask_cfg.c L264, L265 and L269 in FTSK_RunUserCodeCyclic10ms.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Two elements over the ADC boundary, read from adc.h and adc.c at 308028fb. The boundary is a three-state conversion sequence driven by a 10 ms task, and the record records that the sequence is time-triggered from the same task function that also drives the power-path switches and the SBC, so a latency in one of those is visible in the others' cycle budget.
